observatories.name: Chandra X-ray Observatory
observatories.summary: One of NASA's Great Observatories and its most powerful X-ray telescope, detecting X-rays from matter superheated by gravity, magnetic fields and explosions.

observatories.name: Euclid
observatories.summary: Investigates dark matter and dark energy by measuring the expansion of the universe and the distribution of dark matter over cosmic time.

observatories.name: EXCITE (EXoplanet Climate Infrared TElescope)
observatories.orbit: Stratospheric balloon. Test flight from New Mexico, then circumpolar long-duration flights
observatories.summary: Studies the atmospheres of exoplanets during long-duration scientific balloon flights.

observatories.name: Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope
observatories.summary: Observes gamma rays from gamma-ray bursts, active galaxies, supernova remnants and pulsars.

science.text: Earlier observations indicated water vapor, sodium and potassium in its atmosphere, alongside Spitzer and other telescopes.

observatories.name: Hubble Space Telescope
observatories.summary: One of NASA's Great Observatories, with a view reaching 13.4 billion light-years, from merging galaxies to the nebulae where stars are born.

observatories.name: International Space Station
observatories.summary: A crewed microgravity laboratory continuously occupied since 2000.

observatories.name: IXPE (Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer)
observatories.summary: Three identical X-ray telescopes detect polarized X-rays from black holes, neutron stars and pulsars.

science.text: NIRSpec made the first clear detection of carbon dioxide in an exoplanet atmosphere.

observatories.name: James Webb Space Telescope
observatories.summary: The largest and most powerful observatory ever launched, observing in infrared, from our solar system to distant worlds and the first galaxies.

observatories.name: Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope
observatories.summary: A wide-field infrared telescope for dark energy, far-off exoplanets and the history of the universe. Its coronagraph will image nearby exoplanets directly.

observatories.name: NICER (Neutron star Interior Composition Explorer)
observatories.orbit: Mounted on the International Space Station
observatories.summary: Studies neutron stars from aboard the space station, and demonstrated navigation using galactic pulsars.

instruments: Two focal plane modules on a deployable mast
observatories.name: NuSTAR (Nuclear Spectroscopic Telescope Array)
observatories.summary: Detects high-energy X-rays from supermassive black holes and the remnants of exploded stars.

observatories.name: Pandora
observatories.summary: A small satellite studying exoplanet atmospheres and the activity of their host stars with long multiwavelength observations, targeting at least 20 planets.

observatories.name: SPHEREx
observatories.summary: Maps the entire sky in near-infrared, observing over 100 million stars and more than 300 million galaxies to build a 3D map of the cosmos.

observatories.name: SuperTIGER (Super Trans-Iron Galactic Element Recorder)
observatories.summary: A balloon-borne instrument measuring cosmic rays from beyond our solar system and galaxy.

observatories.name: TESS (Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite)
observatories.orbit: Highly elliptical Earth orbit, in 2:1 resonance with the Moon
observatories.summary: Designed to detect exoplanets. In its extended observations it also finds asteroids, pulsating stars and supernovae.

observatories.name: XMM Newton (X-ray Multi-Mirror Mission Newton)
observatories.summary: Uses X-ray and optical/ultraviolet telescopes to study objects from solar system planets to distant galaxy clusters.

observatories.name: XRISM (X-ray Imaging and Spectroscopy Mission)
observatories.summary: Studies celestial X-ray sources to learn how the largest structures formed and how matter behaves under extreme gravity.

observatories.name: ASTHROS
observatories.summary: A far-infrared balloon telescope that will make 3D maps of interstellar gas to study stellar feedback.

observatories.name: ATHENA (Advanced Telescope for High-ENergy Astrophysics)
observatories.summary: A planned X-ray observatory investigating how ordinary matter assembles into galaxies and how black holes grow.

observatories.name: COSI (Compton Spectrometer and Imager)
observatories.summary: A gamma-ray telescope that will study the creation and destruction of matter and antimatter, and the final stages of stars.

observatories.name: EXCLAIM (Experiment for Cryogenic Large-Aperture Intensity Mapping)
observatories.summary: A far-infrared balloon telescope that will map how stars and galaxies formed over time.

model.note: A 2006 design concept, not the current spacecraft.

observatories.name: LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna)
observatories.orbit: Planned orbit around the Sun, trailing Earth
observatories.summary: Will detect gravitational waves from events such as merging massive black holes.

observatories.name: ASCA (Advanced Satellite for Cosmology and Astrophysics)
observatories.summary: An X-ray spacecraft that studied distant active galaxies and the cosmic X-ray background.

observatories.name: BurstCube
observatories.summary: A CubeSat for short gamma-ray bursts and neutron star mergers.

observatories.name: CGRO (Compton Gamma-Ray Observatory)
observatories.summary: One of NASA's Great Observatories, it found blazars and mapped radioactive aluminum across the Milky Way.

observatories.name: COBE (Cosmic Background Explorer)
observatories.summary: Measured the cosmic microwave background, giving key evidence for the big bang.

observatories.name: GALEX (Galaxy Evolution Explorer)
observatories.summary: Performed the first all-sky ultraviolet survey.

observatories.name: HaloSat
observatories.summary: A student-led CubeSat that studied the hot gas halo of the Milky Way.

observatories.name: Hitomi
observatories.summary: An X-ray observatory for the evolution of the universe and dark matter in galaxy clusters.

observatories.name: INTEGRAL (International Gamma-Ray Astrophysics Laboratory)
observatories.orbit: High elliptical Earth orbit during operations
observatories.summary: Observed gamma-ray bursts, supernovae and active galaxies in gamma rays, X-rays and visible light.

observatories.name: Kepler Space Telescope
observatories.orbit: Orbit around the Sun, trailing Earth
observatories.summary: A planet-hunting telescope that observed over half a million stars and revealed there are more planets than stars in our galaxy.

observatories.name: LISA Pathfinder
observatories.summary: Demonstrated technologies required for LISA.

observatories.name: Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory
observatories.summary: Studied gamma-ray bursts with three multiwavelength telescopes.

observatories.name: OAO (Orbiting Astronomical Observatory)
observatories.summary: A four-satellite program, two of them successful, and the direct ancestors of Hubble, Chandra and Swift.

observatories.name: PIPER (Primordial Inflation Polarization Explorer)
observatories.summary: A balloon-borne instrument measuring the polarization of the cosmic microwave background.

observatories.name: Planck
observatories.summary: Made precise measurements of minuscule variations in the cosmic microwave background.

observatories.name: RXTE (Rossi X-ray Timing Explorer)
observatories.summary: Studied the environments around white dwarfs, neutron stars and black holes.

observatories.name: SOFIA (Stratospheric Observatory for Infrared Astronomy)
observatories.orbit: Modified Boeing 747SP in the stratosphere, up to about 45,000 feet
observatories.summary: A flying infrared observatory that collected data on 10-hour overnight flights.

science.text: Earlier observations indicated water vapor, sodium and potassium in its atmosphere, alongside Hubble and other telescopes.

observatories.name: Spitzer Space Telescope
observatories.orbit: Orbit around the Sun, trailing Earth
observatories.summary: The last of NASA's Great Observatories, studying the distant universe, stellar nurseries and planets around other stars in infrared.

observatories.name: Suzaku
observatories.summary: Studied high energy X-ray sources such as supernova explosions and black holes.

observatories.name: WISE/NEOWISE
observatories.summary: Mapped the entire sky in infrared, then was renamed NEOWISE to find near-Earth objects.

observatories.name: WMAP (Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe)
observatories.summary: Measured temperature differences across the cosmic microwave background.

observatories.name: CoRoT
observatories.orbit: Polar low Earth orbit during operations
observatories.summary: An early space transit survey, and among the first to find planets from orbit.

instruments: Astrometry, photometry and spectroscopy on a shared focal plane
observatories.name: Gaia
observatories.summary: Mapped the positions and motions of over a billion stars with extreme precision.

observatories.name: CHEOPS (CHaracterising ExOPlanets Satellite)
observatories.summary: Measures the sizes of known exoplanets by watching them transit bright stars.

unattributed.facility: University of Canterbury Mt John Observatory
